label: Frame generation
desc: Turn the layer on or off while playing. Off: frames pass through unchanged.

label: Target FPS
desc: Frame rate to aim for: your screen's refresh rate (90 on the Deck OLED). The slider goes to 120 or your refresh rate, if higher.

label: Most generated frames
desc: Most extra frames inserted between two game frames. Should be at least target FPS / game FPS - 1. Up to 10 with Experimental on; above 4, set it, then restart the game (the swapchain is built for the value at game start).

label: Game FPS cap (0 = off)
desc: Limits the game's own frame rate. Use your Target FPS divided by a whole number (45 or 30 for 90, 30 for 60) so the generated frames come out evenly. 0 = no limit.
greyWhy: Frame generation is off, so no cap applies.

label: Bypass margin
desc: Frames are added only when target FPS / game FPS is at least this value (1.01 = 1 % faster). Higher: the layer switches off sooner when the game is nearly fast enough.

label: Phase lock
desc: Aligns generated frames with the game's frames for even spacing, when the ratio of Target FPS to the game's frame rate is close to a whole number.
greyWhy: Not used when generation is off or in low-latency mode.

label: Phase offset
desc: Where generated frames sit between two game frames. 0.5 = halfway; 0 = one on the game frame itself.
greyWhy: Needs phase lock, and is not used in low-latency mode.

label: Two-sided interpolation (experimental)
desc: Uses motion from both neighbouring game frames. Can reduce smearing at object edges; costs more GPU time.
greyWhy: Needs optical flow, and is not used in low-latency mode.

label: Optical flow
desc: Moves the in-between frames along the motion between two game frames. Off: a plain cross-fade (no optical-flow passes, ghosts on movement). On costs about 5 ms of GPU time per game frame in the scene we measured on a Steam Deck.
greyWhy: Low-latency mode always uses motion, so this is on.

label: Low-latency mode (extrapolate)
desc: Shows each game frame at once and predicts the next ones, so input feels quicker. Predicted frames can look blockier.

label: One-sided fill (experimental)
desc: Behind a moving object, takes the colour from the one frame that shows the background. Offline test (25 frame triplets, CPU flow): worse than the default in 21, better in 4, on pixels where the two frames differ (average +6 % error). For testing, not an improvement. Needs Experimental and a game restart.

label: Keep HUD still (0 = off)
desc: Keeps still parts such as the HUD from being dragged by motion. Default 0.08; 0.03 suits grainy games; 0 = off. Too high freezes real movement.

label: Motion detail (1 = finest)
desc: How finely motion is detected. 1: sharpest, most GPU time. 3: coarsest, cheapest.

label: Command buffers
desc: How far the layer may queue ahead of the GPU. 8 is fine; 16 showed no gain in our tests. Higher adds a little latency.

label: Synthetic margin
desc: Least distance, as a share of the interval between two game frames, between a shown frame and a game frame. 0 lets one sit on the game frame (sharper at times); that saves a pass only with phase lock on, Phase offset 0 and steady frame times. Applies from the next pair.

label: Experimental
desc: Unlocks the settings below and lets Most generated frames reach 10 (4 otherwise). Read at game start: turn it on, then restart the game. Untested: can add latency, glitches or crashes.
